Verdict: ACCEPTThe three requested claims are mathematically sound:The general fusion ledger correctly counts module–selection incidences, including repeated consumption of the same physical site.The protected-donor argument and the degree-four nonduplication inequality  $K_{\mathrm{in}}+L\le d_4$  are valid.The opposed-band construction proves the claimed obstruction for every even  $w\ge6$  and even  $h\ge4$ . Its feasibility, physical counts, four alignment phases, and ordered mixed-bundle freezing certificate all check.The obstruction has exactly the stated scope: automatic validity of  $d_4\le S+2J$  fails, with unbounded excess. The coarse condition remains sufficient when it holds. The opposed bands satisfy the finer condition  $K_{\mathrm{in}}+L\le S+2J$ , and their actual target slack is strictly positive.My assessment below follows the coordinate definitions and symbolic proofs in the attachment. The finite controls, historical verdicts, and Lean receipts are not premises of this verdict. References distinguish the first note, “Degree-three fusion,” from the second, “Opposed bands.”    physical-fusion-opposed-bands1. The general physical fusion ledger is exact1.1 The required local facts survive the degree-four extensionThe relevant feasibility rule is that a selected site has at most one occupied neighbor. Original supports have their specified unique endpoint neighbor. All endpoints under consideration have occupied degree at least three.These conditions give both local facts used in the ledger.Endpoint connectivity inside a unit square. The only disconnected nonempty subset of the four-cycle is a pair of opposite corners. If those corners were endpoints, either remaining corner, if occupied, would be selected and would touch both endpoints. Thus both remaining corners must be blank. Each endpoint would then have at most its two neighbors outside the square occupied, contradicting occupied degree at least three.Receiver locality. Suppose a selected corner  $x$  lies in an endpoint-bearing square but its unique endpoint neighbor lies outside that square. Any endpoint inside the square must be opposite  $x$ . The two intervening corners are neighbors of  $x$ , so they must be blank. Again, the opposite endpoint would have occupied degree at most two.Neither argument requires occupied degree exactly three. This justifies their continued use in the degree-four ledger.1.2 Neighbor preservation and the four-module square lemma are correctAt final occupied degree three,
$$A_i\subseteq A,\qquad
|N(p)\cap A_i|=|N(p)\cap A|=3$$
for every  $p\in P_i$ . Therefore
$$N(p)\cap A_i=N(p)\cap A.$$
In particular, if  $p\in P_i$  and a foreign endpoint  $v\in P_j$  are adjacent, then  $v\in T_i$ , and symmetrically  $p\in T_j$ .The proof that a mixed full square must use four different modules exhausts the possibilities:Two opposite corners from one module violate its original local endpoint connectivity.Three corners from one module would force the fourth corner to have been a selection touching two original endpoints.Two adjacent corners from one module would force the other two corners to have been adjacent selections, each already touching an endpoint.Thus a mixed full square has four module labels. At each corner, its two square-neighbors were original selections, while its matching mate was an original endpoint outside the square. Its original endpoint degree was therefore one.The packet correctly confines this restriction to final degree three. It does not impose it in the degree-four extension.1.3 The tile correction is correct even when contraction produces parallel edgesFor a final receiver tile  $Q$ , write: $m_Q$  for the number of represented original modules; $e_Q$  for the number of intratile foreign endpoint edges; $j_Q=1$  if the tile is full and mixed, and  $0$  otherwise.Then
$$e_Q=m_Q-1+j_Q.$$
A direct edge count makes this independent of any convention about contracted multigraphs.If the final endpoint subset is not full, it is a tree. Each represented original subset is connected and proper, hence also a tree. Subtracting the original internal edges from the final edges gives  $m_Q-1$ .If the tile is full and mixed, every original subset is proper, so
$$e_Q
=4-\sum_i\bigl(|P_i\cap Q|-1\bigr)
=m_Q.$$
If the tile is full and belongs to one module,  $e_Q=0$ .Consequently, with  $E_{\mathrm{in}}=\sum_Qe_Q$ ,
$$|R|=\sum_i|R_i|-E_{\mathrm{in}}+J.$$
This covers mixed full tiles with two, three, or four represented modules in the degree-four case.1.4 Shared consumed supports introduce no missing termThe exact object being counted before fusion is an incidence
$$(i,x),\qquad x\in T_i\cap V(R_i).$$
If  $x$  becomes an endpoint, its unique original anchor  $p\in P_i$  lies in the same tile, by original locality. Thus consumed receiver incidences correspond bijectively to oriented intratile foreign edges
$$p\longrightarrow x
\quad\text{with }x\in T_i.$$
This is precisely why a physical site selected by two original modules must be removed twice from the sum of original receiver-selection counts. Those are two different incidences, with two different anchors.At final degree three, both orientations of every intratile foreign edge have an original support incidence. Hence
$$t_R=\sum_i t_i-2E_{\mathrm{in}}.$$
In the degree-four extension, an orientation lacks that incidence exactly when the foreign neighbor was originally blank at its tail endpoint. Each such endpoint has exactly one new occupied neighbor, so the missing intratile incidences are counted exactly by  $K_{\mathrm{in}}$ . Therefore
$$\boxed{t_R=\sum_i t_i-2E_{\mathrm{in}}+K_{\mathrm{in}}.}$$
There are also no hidden retained-selection corrections:A retained selection cannot belong to two modules, because their disjoint endpoint sets would supply two different surviving anchors.A retained selection cannot newly enter a receiver tile containing only foreign endpoints: final locality would put its old surviving anchor inside that tile.Extra selections are expressly outside the original receiver union.Since matching edges add without duplication, substitution gives
$$\boxed{\rho_{\mathrm{final}}
=\sum_i\rho_i-2J+K_{\mathrm{in}}.}$$
At degree three,  $K_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ . Connectedness of each original module and tile ownership also justify the componentwise statement.These arguments validate the exact identities in the first note’s §§4 and 8, including the repeated-support issue.    physical-fusion-opposed-bands2. Protected donors and degree-four nonduplication are valid2.1 The straight-anchor argument preserves the actual selectionNormalize the anchor to  $p=(0,0)$ , its opposite endpoint neighbors to  $(-1,0),(1,0)$ , and the supported selection to  $x=(0,1)$ .The sites  $(-1,1),(1,1)$  are originally blank because they neighbor  $x$ , which already touches  $p$ . Degree preservation at  $(-1,0),(1,0)$  keeps both blank.If  $x$  became an endpoint, only  $p$  and  $(0,2)$  could be occupied neighbors. This contradicts the minimum final endpoint degree of three.This observation also confirms the degree-four version: the argument needs degree preservation at the two protecting endpoints, not at every endpoint of the module.For the full donor tile, final feasibility keeps the two corners adjacent to  $x$  blank, and degree preservation at the guard  $q$  keeps the opposite corner blank. The tile therefore has exactly one selected site and no endpoint. Its physical deficit is exactly one.Two protected donor tiles from different modules cannot coincide: their unique selected sites would coincide, and that retained site would have two different original anchors.2.2 The necessary charge signs follow from the supplied constructorsFor a two-leg module with even leg heights  $a,b$ , put

The receiver-tile counts are five in phase  $(0,0)$  and four in the other phases, giving charges  $-2,0,0,0$ .Therefore
$$S=N_+-\sum_i\rho_i\ge0$$
has the claimed meaning for the entire stated two-leg/rotor class.2.3 The nonduplication proof is an injection into degree-four endpointsThe protecting endpoints and their unique original blank neighbors are:ProtectorUnique original blank neighborLocation relative to protector’s tile $q=(1,3)$  $(2,3)$ Outside $a=(2,1)$  $(2,2)$ Outside $b=(4,1)$  $(4,2)$ OutsideThe minimum leg height four causes no exception. Although  $b=(4,1)$  is then a leaf, it still has the stated unique blank neighbor.Choose one degree-four protector from each marked positive module. The chosen endpoints are distinct because original endpoint sets are disjoint. Their new-neighbor events are intertile, so none is counted in  $K_{\mathrm{in}}$ . Hence
$$\boxed{K_{\mathrm{in}}+L\le d_4.}$$
This remains valid even if different chosen events point toward a common physical site: the injection is into the tail endpoints counted by  $d_4$ .Every unmarked positive module retains its distinct physical unit donor, so
$$D\ge N_+-L.$$
Combining this with the exact ledger gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma
&=D-\rho_{\mathrm{final}}\\
&\ge (N_+-L)-\left(\sum_i\rho_i-2J+K_{\mathrm{in}}\right)\\
&=\boxed{S+2J-K_{\mathrm{in}}-L}\\
&\ge S+2J-d_4.
\end{aligned}$$
Both sufficient criteria follow correctly.Two distinctions are preserved throughout: $L$  counts marked modules; it is not asserted to equal the exact number of destroyed donor tiles in every fusion.A new full tile contributes through  $-2J$  in the receiver charge. It is never reused as an endpoint-free donor.3. The opposed-band physical construction and exact counts checkFor every stated  $w,h$ , the two endpoint sets in the second note’s §2 are disjoint. Applying the source constructors and removing consumed supports gives exactly
$$\begin{aligned}
T={}&\{(-1,0),(-1,w+1)\}\\
&\cup\{(r,-1),(r,w+2):r=0,2,\ldots,h+2\}\\
&\cup\{(r,2),(r,w-1):r=3,5,\ldots,h-1\}.

Every site in the first two groups has exactly its designated  $B$ -endpoint neighbor. Every site in the last group has exactly its designated  $A$ -endpoint neighbor.The separation arguments are uniform:The two interior columns differ by  $w-3\ge3$ .Successive selections in each listed column are two rows apart.The exterior and interior groups cannot acquire cross-group occupied neighbors.At  $h=4$ , the interior progression still contains row three.At  $w=6$ , the interior columns remain separated by three.The occupied coordinate ranges are exactly within rows  $-1,\ldots,h+2$  and columns  $-1,\ldots,w+2$ , so translation by  $(1,1)$  fits the claimed even rectangle.3.1 Every foreign edge and degree-four event is accounted forThe foreign endpoint edges are precisely
$$(r,0)--(r,1),\quad(r,w)--(r,w+1),
\qquad 0\le r\le h,$$
and
$$(h,1)--(h+1,1),\quad(h,w)--(h+1,w).$$
Each edge has exactly one orientation whose foreign neighbor was originally blank:ContactEndpoint receiving the new-neighbor eventSide contact at odd row $A$ -endpointSide contact at even row $B$ -endpointCap contact $B$ -endpoint at row  $h+1$ Thus
$$d_4=h+(h+2)+2=\boxed{2h+4}.$$
The other foreign orientations replace original selected supports.3.2 The canonical alignment has  $J=K_{\mathrm{in}}=0$ After translation by  $(1,1)$ , the side contacts cross column-tile boundaries  $1|2$  and  $w+1|w+2$ . The cap contacts cross the row-tile boundary  $h+1|h+2$ .Therefore every new-neighbor event is intertile:
$$K_{\mathrm{in}}=0.$$
Every mixed full unit square uses a side seam, so none is an aligned physical tile:
$$J=0.$$
The transported positive module  $B$  has its canonical donor selection consumed. Its two stem protectors become degree four; its guard does not. Because  $L$  counts modules, this gives  $L=1$ , not two.3.3 The receiver and area counts have a direct geometric derivationThe total counts are
$$|P|=4w+4h+4,\qquad
|M|=2w+2h+2,\qquad
|T|=2h+4.$$
In the canonical alignment, three tile-row groups contain a bar; each contributes  $w/2+2$  receiver tiles. The remaining  $h/2-1$  groups contain only stems, contributing four receiver tiles each. Hence
$$|R|
=3\left(\frac w2+2\right)+4\left(\frac h2-1\right)
=\boxed{\frac{3w}{2}+2h+2}.$$
Every retained selection lies in a receiver, so
$$t_R=2h+4$$
and
$$\rho=t_R+|M|-2|R|=\boxed{2-w}.$$
Direct area subtraction gives
$$\boxed{\sigma=\frac{h(w-4)}2+2}.$$
Every endpoint-free tile in this alignment is completely empty. Counting those tiles gives
$$\boxed{D=\frac{(w-4)(h-2)}2}.$$

$$\sigma=D+w-2\ge w-2>0.$$
These physical counts independently agree with the fusion ledger; they do not depend on treating that ledger as the only route to the numerical result.    physical-fusion-opposed-bands4. Cap contacts are intratile exactly when  $a=0$ . Since each foreign edge here has exactly one new-neighbor orientation,

=2(h+1)(1-b)+2(1-a).}$$

Every stage of the uniform opposed-band freezing certificate is valid5.1 The induction handles simultaneous mixed bundlesLet  $m$  be the actual matching involution, and let  $X$  be an arbitrary set of promoted endpoints, allowing both colors and both ends of a matching edge. Its occupied set after promotion is
$$A_X
=
T\cup X\cup
V\!\left(M\setminus\{e\in M:e\cap X\ne\varnothing\}\right).$$
If an earlier frozen endpoint  $v$  is excluded from  $X$ , then  $m(v)$  remains occupied:If  $m(v)\in X$ , it remains as a selected site.Otherwise neither end of that matching edge is promoted, so the edge remains.Therefore, if  $F$  is the already frozen set,
$$T\cup m(F)\subseteq A_X$$
for every bundle avoiding  $F$ .An endpoint with two distinct neighbors in this set cannot be promoted, because it would become selected with at least two occupied neighbors.This is the correct mixed-bundle induction. $$(h+2,o)=m_B(h+2,i),
\qquad
(h+1,i)=m_B(h+1,j),$$

\qquad
(h+1,i)=m_B(h+1,j),$$

and
$$\rho=24+(4w+12)-2(2w+17)=2.$$

Hence no perfect matching can use a foreign edge. $$J=2,\quad K_{\mathrm{in}}=4,\quad L=0,\quad
\rho=2-w,\quad \sigma=6w-12.$$

$$S=5,\qquad J=K_{\mathrm{in}}=0,\qquad L=1,\qquad d_4=2h+4.$$
Therefore
$$d_4-(S+2J)=2h-1\longrightarrow\infty,$$
while
$$K_{\mathrm{in}}+L=1\le5=S+2J.$$

$$N_+-L-B\ge \rho_{\mathrm{final}}-B$$
such units. The subsequent exclusion of the  $q=5$  motifs invokes a first-failure classification whose definitions and proof are not reproduced here.
